title: Reference
description: A schema node whose only effective content is a $ref keyword holding a URI or JSON Pointer fragment (e.g. '#/definitions/Address') that delegates validation of an instance to another schema, adding no constraints of its own. A usage site that points at a type declared elsewhere, not the declaration of that type. Use SchemaDefinition instead when the element is the named, reusable type being pointed at (the target under 'definitions'), rather than the pointer to it. Use SchemaProperty instead when the element is a named property of an object schema that also carries its own type, description, default or other constraints, even if it uses $ref to obtain its type. Use SchemaComposition instead when the $ref must be combined with further constraints or alternatives, which in Draft 7 requires wrapping it in allOf/anyOf/oneOf. Use JSONSchema instead when the element is the whole root schema document with $schema and $id, not a pointer into or toward one.

$ref.description: URI or JSON Pointer fragment referencing another schema

x-dr-standard: JSON Schema Draft 7 (draft-handrews-json-schema-01) §8.3 Schema References With "$ref"
x-dr-evidence: A literal "$ref": "#/definitions/..." or "$ref": "other.schema.json#/..." entry in a JSON/YAML schema or an OpenAPI components file
A field in a DTO, Pydantic model or TypeScript interface typed by another separately declared model class (e.g. 'billing: Address'), which schema generators emit as a $ref

Schema-generator configuration or decorators that hoist nested types into shared definitions, such as Pydantic's ref_template, zod-to-json-schema $refStrategy, or @ApiProperty({ type: () => Address })
